\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قطيع} (qaṭīʿ)}{قطيع (qaṭīʿ)}]{\ar{قطيع} (qaṭīʿ) — a herd; a flock}

\label{lesson:AR-C478-qati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for pure, then the Arabic for a strait.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قطيع}}
\textbf{\ar{قطيع}} — \emph{qaṭīʿ} — \textquotedblleft{}a herd; a flock\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رأينا} \ar{قطيعا} \ar{من} \ar{الغزلان}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raʾaynā qaṭīʿan min al-ghizlān.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We saw a herd of gazelles.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قطيع}} (\emph{qaṭīʿ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-ṭ-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to cut\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A herd is a portion cut off from the rest.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qaṭīʿ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qaṭīʿ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raʾaynā qaṭīʿan min al-ghizlān.} — We saw a herd of gazelles.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for pure, then the Arabic for a strait, then say \emph{qaṭīʿ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{قطيع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A herd; a flock\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مرعى} (marʿā)}{مرعى (marʿā)}]{\ar{مرعى} (marʿā) — a pasture}

\label{lesson:AR-C478-mara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a strait, then the Arabic for a herd.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مرعى}}
\textbf{\ar{مرعى}} — \emph{marʿā} — \textquotedblleft{}a pasture\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ذهب} \ar{القطيع} \ar{إلى} \ar{المرعى}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dhahaba al-qaṭīʿ ilā al-marʿā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The herd went to the pasture.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مرعى}} (\emph{marʿā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-ʿ-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to pasture, to tend\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The pattern \emph{mafʿal} makes it the place of grazing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marʿā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marʿā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhahaba al-qaṭīʿ ilā al-marʿā.} — The herd went to the pasture.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a strait, then the Arabic for a herd, then say \emph{marʿā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مرعى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A pasture\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قفص} (qafaṣ)}{قفص (qafaṣ)}]{\ar{قفص} (qafaṣ) — a cage}

\label{lesson:AR-C478-qafas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a herd, then the Arabic for a pasture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قفص}}
\textbf{\ar{قفص}} — \emph{qafaṣ} — \textquotedblleft{}a cage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الببغاء} \ar{في} \ar{قفص} \ar{صغير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-babbaghāʾ fī qafaṣ ṣaghīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The parrot was in a small cage.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أقفاص}, \emph{aqfāṣ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قفص}} (\emph{qafaṣ}) is linked by EtymDB to Aramaic \emph{qupsā}, a word usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}a box, a basket\textquotedblright{}; the details of the borrowing are not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qafaṣ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qafaṣ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-babbaghāʾ fī qafaṣ ṣaghīr.} — The parrot was in a small cage.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a herd, then the Arabic for a pasture, then say \emph{qafaṣ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فرو} (farw)}{فرو (farw)}]{\ar{فرو} (farw) — fur}

\label{lesson:AR-C478-farw}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a pasture, then the Arabic for a cage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فرو}}
\textbf{\ar{فرو}} — \emph{farw} — \textquotedblleft{}fur\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{للثعلب} \ar{فرو} \ar{جميل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{li-th-thaʿlab farw jamīl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fox has beautiful fur.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فرو}} (\emph{farw}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{f-r-w}, \textquotedblleft{}fur, a fur coat\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-th-thaʿlab farw jamīl.} — The fox has beautiful fur.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رعى} (raʿā)}{رعى (raʿā)}]{\ar{رعى} (raʿā) — to graze; to tend (animals)}

\label{lesson:AR-C478-raa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a cage, then the Arabic for fur.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رعى}}
\textbf{\ar{رعى}} — \emph{raʿā} — \textquotedblleft{}to graze; to tend (animals)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ترعى} \ar{الأبقار} \ar{في} \ar{الحقل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tarʿā al-abqār fī al-ḥaql.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cows graze in the field.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرعى}, \emph{yarʿā}.

A shepherd is \emph{rāʿī}, the one who tends.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رعى}} (\emph{raʿā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-ʿ-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to pasture, to tend\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the plain verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raʿā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raʿā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarʿā al-abqār fī al-ḥaql.} — The cows graze in the field.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a cage, then the Arabic for fur, then say \emph{raʿā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 471–478 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R478-review-471-478}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a gulf and an ocean.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a gulf, an ocean, coral, a current, depth
  \item a rock, a plateau, a summit, a slope, an edge
  \item an oasis, a mirage, a jungle, a swamp, barren
  \item a falcon, an ostrich, a seagull, a feather, to float
  \item a hyena, a cheetah, a hedgehog, a squirrel, a bat
  \item a scorpion, a locust, moss, a claw, to prey on
  \item a shark, a crab, oysters, pure, a strait
  \item a herd, a pasture, a cage, fur, to graze
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A gulf? (\textbf{\ar{خليج}}, \emph{khalīj}.) An ocean? (\textbf{\ar{محيط}}, \emph{muḥīṭ}.) Coral? (\textbf{\ar{مرجان}}, \emph{marjān}.) A current? (\textbf{\ar{تيار}}, \emph{tayyār}.) Depth? (\textbf{\ar{عمق}}, \emph{ʿumq}.) A rock? (\textbf{\ar{صخرة}}, \emph{ṣakhra}.) A plateau? (\textbf{\ar{هضبة}}, \emph{haḍba}.) A summit? (\textbf{\ar{قمة}}, \emph{qimma}.) A slope? (\textbf{\ar{منحدر}}, \emph{munḥadar}.) An edge? (\textbf{\ar{حافة}}, \emph{ḥāffa}.) An oasis? (\textbf{\ar{واحة}}, \emph{wāḥa}.) A mirage? (\textbf{\ar{سراب}}, \emph{sarāb}.) A jungle? (\textbf{\ar{أدغال}}, \emph{adghāl}.) A swamp? (\textbf{\ar{مستنقع}}, \emph{mustanqaʿ}.) Barren? (\textbf{\ar{قاحل}}, \emph{qāḥil}.) A falcon? (\textbf{\ar{صقر}}, \emph{ṣaqr}.) An ostrich? (\textbf{\ar{نعامة}}, \emph{naʿāma}.) A seagull? (\textbf{\ar{نورس}}, \emph{nawras}.) A feather? (\textbf{\ar{ريشة}}, \emph{rīsha}.) To float? (\textbf{\ar{طفا}}, \emph{ṭafā}.) A hyena? (\textbf{\ar{ضبع}}, \emph{ḍabʿ}.) A cheetah? (\textbf{\ar{فهد}}, \emph{fahd}.) A hedgehog? (\textbf{\ar{قنفذ}}, \emph{qunfudh}.) A squirrel? (\textbf{\ar{سنجاب}}, \emph{sinjāb}.) A bat? (\textbf{\ar{خفاش}}, \emph{khuffāsh}.) A scorpion? (\textbf{\ar{عقرب}}, \emph{ʿaqrab}.) A locust? (\textbf{\ar{جرادة}}, \emph{jarāda}.) Moss? (\textbf{\ar{طحلب}}, \emph{ṭuḥlub}.) A claw? (\textbf{\ar{مخلب}}, \emph{mikhlab}.) To prey on? (\textbf{\ar{افترس}}, \emph{iftarasa}.) A shark? (\textbf{\ar{قرش}}, \emph{qirsh}.) A crab? (\textbf{\ar{سلطعون}}, \emph{salṭaʿūn}.) Oysters? (\textbf{\ar{محار}}, \emph{maḥār}.) Pure? (\textbf{\ar{نقي}}, \emph{naqī}.) A strait? (\textbf{\ar{مضيق}}, \emph{maḍīq}.) A herd? (\textbf{\ar{قطيع}}, \emph{qaṭīʿ}.) A pasture? (\textbf{\ar{مرعى}}, \emph{marʿā}.) A cage? (\textbf{\ar{قفص}}, \emph{qafaṣ}.) Fur? (\textbf{\ar{فرو}}, \emph{farw}.) To graze? (\textbf{\ar{رعى}}, \emph{raʿā}.)
